article.headline: Games To Watch: Unbeaten starts collide at Clinton and MRA
article.html:
Unbeaten starts meet on the soccer field in Clinton and on the basketball court at Madison-Ridgeland Academy Monday. Clinton’s girls bring a 4–0 record into their match with 5–0–1 Northwest Rankin, while MRA and visiting Houston, Tennessee, each enter their boys basketball game at 3–0.

The remaining November 23, 2026, schedule also includes an unbeaten Potts Camp boys team at the Hickory Flat Thanksgiving Tournament and several other strong early records facing tests. All times below are Central Standard Time. These are selected upcoming varsity fixtures, with entering records checked on their matchup pages; earlier games are omitted.

Clinton and Northwest Rankin put unbeaten soccer records together

The 7 p.m. girls soccer match at Clinton is one of the clearest tests of unbeaten form on the remaining slate. Northwest Rankin has five wins and a draw, while the Arrows have won all four of their reported matches. Neither carries a defeat into the nonconference meeting, so both have a loss-free opening to protect.

The schools’ boys teams meet earlier, at 5 p.m.. Northwest Rankin is listed at 3–3 and Clinton at 2–3–1. Their records give the boys fixture a different emphasis: the Cougars can move above an even record, while the Arrows can draw level in wins and losses. Both matches are listed as nonconference.

West Lauderdale’s girls take a perfect start to Brandon

West Lauderdale’s girls are 8–0 ahead of their 5:30 p.m. match at Brandon. The Bulldogs enter 6–3, providing a winning opponent for a Knights team that has yet to lose a reported game. The nonconference trip gives West Lauderdale an opportunity to extend its perfect opening against a team with several victories of its own.

The 7:15 p.m. boys match pairs West Lauderdale at 5–4–1 with Brandon at 3–4–1. The Knights have a winning record to defend, while the Bulldogs can balance their wins and losses. Both schools therefore have a distinct early-season marker at stake across the soccer doubleheader.

MRA hosts Houston in an unbeaten boys basketball matchup

Madison-Ridgeland Academy hosts the Houston Mustangs of Germantown, Tennessee, at 4:30 p.m.. Both teams are listed at 3–0. The fixture is identified with the MRA Turkey Shootout and listed as nonconference, bringing together two perfect openings for an interstate test in Madison.

West Union and Oxford protect perfect basketball starts

West Union’s boys enter 6–0 for the 4:30 p.m. game against Holly Springs, which is listed at 1–4. The Eagles’ unbeaten record makes them the team to measure against in this matchup. The game is a neutral-site tournament fixture at the New Albany Thanksgiving Classic, rather than a regular home game at either school.

Oxford’s girls are also 6–0, with Jackson Prep visiting at 5:30 p.m. for a game in the Charger Invitational. Prep enters 5–2. That combination gives the Chargers a winning opponent as they try to preserve their perfect start, with the Patriots seeking a road tournament victory against an unbeaten team.

Booneville has unbeaten records in both basketball divisions

Booneville’s girls enter the 6 p.m. game against Center Hill at 2–0. The visiting Mustangs are listed at 3–2. Center Hill has a winning record of its own to build on, while the Blue Devils have an unbeaten opening to defend in the nonconference meeting.

The boys game follows at 7:30 p.m. against New Hope. Both teams are listed at 1–0, making this another matchup between sides without a reported loss. Their limited early records do not establish a long run of form, but the meeting offers a direct comparison as each tries to build on a winning start.

Potts Camp brings a perfect start to Hickory Flat

Potts Camp’s boys meet East Union at 6 p.m. in the Hickory Flat Thanksgiving Tournament. The Cardinals enter 5–0 and the Urchins 1–3. The game is listed as neutral-site and nonconference. Potts Camp can extend its unbeaten start, while East Union has an opportunity to challenge a team that has won every reported game so far.

Horn Lake and Cleveland Central bring matching records

Horn Lake hosts Cleveland Central at 6 p.m. in girls basketball, with both teams listed at 6–1. The Eagles are coming off Saturday’s 51–36 loss at Greenwood, so this is a chance to respond against another team with only one reported defeat. That result is covered in our Saturday varsity recap. The fixture is identified with Horn Lake’s MS/TN Challenge.

Pontotoc faces an Alabama opponent; Hancock hosts Tupelo

Pontotoc’s boys face Florence, Alabama, at 4:30 p.m. in a neutral-site game at the Booneville High School Thanksgiving Tournament. Both teams are listed at 3–1. Their matching records make this a useful interstate comparison, with each entering the tournament fixture with more wins than losses.

Hancock’s girls bring a 6–0 record to the 6 p.m. game against Tupelo in Kiln. The Golden Wave enter 1–2. Hancock has a perfect start to protect at home, while Tupelo can reach an even record by winning the nonconference game.
